examples.trans: Don't you yell at me! I told you in plain Russian.

meanings.en: to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ледить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on', paired with 'проследить'.

examples.trans: Keep an eye on the child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ражение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'expression' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня такое же глупое выражение лица было.
examples.trans: I had the exact same foolish expression on my face.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть выражение.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always expression.

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'suit; costume' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is wearing a new dark suit.

examples.text: Звать клиентов в детское кафе. В костюме вафельного рожка.
examples.trans: Call customers into a children's café. In a waffle-cone costume.

Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'портить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to spoil, ruin, damage', paired with 'портить'.

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.
Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'year' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'gobble, devour'.

examples.text: Он теперь год здесь жрать должен.
examples.trans: Now he owes me a whole year of business here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
